title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
input_format:
The first line contains `N`.
The next `N` lines each contain two integers `start` and `end`.
output_format: Print each merged interval on a new line as `start end`.

starter_code.python:
# Merge Intervals
# Input:
# Line 1: n (number of intervals)
# Next n lines: start end

n = int(input())
intervals = []
for _ in range(n):
    intervals.append(list(map(int, input().split())))

# Write your code below:

hints.text: Sort the intervals by their start times `intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])`.
Iterate through intervals: if the current interval starts after the previous ends, add it as a new interval.
Otherwise, merge them by updating `previous.end = max(previous.end, current.end)`.
